children: Local AI assistant QClaw said on its homepage on September 24 that it will stop accepting new user registrations effective immediately and will officially shut down on December 24 due to business adjustments. According to ChainCatcher, the company said it will support user data migration and provide points subsidies to users who migrate.

Tencent introduced QClaw on March 10 as part of its “Longxia” product lineup, which also included WorkBuddy, Tencent Cloud Lighthouse, the ADP intelligent agent development platform, and Tencent Cloud Desktop. Tencent said at the time that QClaw was in beta testing.

Tencent described QClaw as a local AI assistant based on OpenClaw that supports one-click installation on Windows and Mac. It can also be remotely controlled through WeChat conversations, allowing users to send commands from their phones so the assistant can operate a computer and return the results.

title: QClaw to Stop New User Registrations and Shut Down on December 24
